ACCESS: https://www.oliverbonas.com/robots.txt fetched FIRST via probe.fetch (HTTP 200, profile edge101). It has a SINGLE group, 'User-agent: *', and names NO anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web or Claude agent; no Crawl-delay, no Content-Signal line. That group disallows /_=_, /basket, /checkout, /checkout/login, /checkout/success, /account, /search, /wishlist and the same eight paths again under the /ie/ and /us/ locale prefixes, plus the patterns /*.php$ and /*.html$. I requested none of them - no internal search, no account/basket/wishlist path, no .php or .html URL, and only the UK (no-prefix) locale. Declared sitemaps: /sitemap.xml, /ie/sitemap.xml, /us/sitemap.xml. Transport was plain curl_cffi with fingerprint rotation; every page HTTP 200, no Cloudflare challenge, no proxy - same route the prior Furniture and Home-Decor passes used.

TREE - TWO SOURCES, RECONCILED. (1) MEGA-MENU: the Homeware mega-menu is fully server-rendered in the SSR HTML of every page; I parsed it off /homeware/by-room/bathroom (267 distinct nav links). Its columns are New In / All Homeware / Bestsellers; Home Accessories (Wall Art, Vases, Mirrors, Lighting, Photo Frames, Plant Pots, Home Decor); Kitchen & Dining (Tableware, Glassware, Mugs, Bar Accessories); Home Fragrance (Candles, Diffusers, Candle Holders); Home Furnishings (Cushions, Quilts, Throws & Blankets, Rugs, Bedding, BATH MATS, Doormats); and SHOP BY ROOM (BATHROOM -> /homeware/by-room/bathroom, Bedroom -> /homeware/category/bedroom-accessories, Kitchen & Dining, Home Office, Living Room, Hallway). 'Bathroom' in Shop by Room is Oliver Bonas's own and only Bathroom entry point. (2) SITEMAP: https://www.oliverbonas.com/sitemap.xml fetched in full (HTTP 200, 4,589,289 bytes, 6,702 <loc> entries covering categories and every PDP). It publishes 113 homeware category / by-room / soft-furnishings nodes, which I read out in full; grepping all 6,702 for bath|bathroom|shower|basin|sink|toilet|tap|vanit|sanitar|wc|soap|toothbrush|towel|mirror|wash surfaces exactly THREE bathroom-classifiable CATEGORY nodes - /homeware/by-room/bathroom, /homeware/category/soap-dispensers-dishes and /homeware/category/bath-mats - plus the individual bathroom PDPs that sit inside them. NOTE ON A TRAP: https://www.oliverbonas.com/bath is NOT a category - it is the Bath, Somerset STORE page (<title> 'Bath | Oliver Bonas', H1 'Bath Oliver Bonas Store'); it was fetched and rejected. There is no bathroom node anywhere under /furniture either (its tree is Seating, Tables, Storage Furniture, Drinks Trolleys - no vanity units, no bathroom cabinets), so the dispatch-note Option-1 concern about Furniture-owned vanities does not arise on this SR.

BREADCRUMB PROOF OF SHAPE: every node's JSON-LD BreadcrumbList was read. 'Homeware | Bathroom Accessories', 'Homeware | Soap Dishes & Dispensers', 'Homeware | Bath Mats', 'Homeware | Storage Hooks', 'Homeware | Mirrors'. They are all DEPTH-2 SIBLINGS of one another, not a parent/child chain, so rule 24 never fires: no recorded URL is a parent of another recorded URL, and the 'Home Decor / Bath Mats / Soap Dishes & Dispensers / Bath & Body / Makeup Bags' strip printed on the Bathroom page is a RELATED-CATEGORY strip (it links to Beauty and to top-level Home Decor), not a child taxonomy - which is why the Bathroom node is itself a terminal listing and correctly carries its own URL.

QTY SOURCE + VERIFICATION: Oliver Bonas's own live result counter is the filters button, rendered literally as 'See all N items'. THREE INDEPENDENT CHECKS, all run this session: (a) EQUIVALENCE - on the three sibling pages that render the number, the number equals the count of <product-listing-wishlist> product tiles in the same SSR grid EXACTLY and on differing sizes: Soap Dishes & Dispensers 'See all 3 items' = 3 tiles, Bath Mats 'See all 13 items' = 13 tiles, Storage Hooks 'See all 30 items' = 30 tiles; also Storage Baskets 13/13, Storage 78/78, Dressing Table Mirrors 7/7, Full Length Mirrors 6/6. That is 7 for 7 today, on top of the 22 for 22 the prior pass on this SR verified. (b) The recorded Bathroom Accessories node renders 'See all items' with NO number in SSR, so its qty comes from that validated tile enumeration: 86 tiles - and independently, extracting every product anchor in the grid and de-duplicating gives 86 UNIQUE product URLs (92 anchors minus the 6 footer links /about-us x5 and /accessories/bags), an exact second-method match. (c) DRIFT - the page was fetched three separate times on rotating fingerprints (chrome120, safari17_0 x2) and returned 86 tiles every time; a WebFetch render independently confirmed the H1 'Bathroom Accessories' and the numberless 'See all items' button. CEILING CHECK: the prior pass proved the SSR grid caps at 100 tiles (demonstrated on /homeware/by-room/home-office, which reports 293 but renders 100); 86 is below the cap and there is no rel=next and no pagination control on the page, so the grid is complete and not truncated. DISCRIMINATION: the counts differ per node (86 / 3 / 13 / 30 / 38 / 78 / 7 / 6), so no site-wide constant is being echoed, and every page's H1 and JSON-LD breadcrumb matched the node requested, so there is no silent parent-serving. Nothing was estimated, no parent number was reused for a child and no quantities were aggregated.

DEDUP: lib/dedup.already_extracted() was run on all 14 candidate URLs (by-room/bathroom, soap-dispensers-dishes, bath-mats, hooks, mirrors and its 3 children, storage, storage-baskets, dressing-table-accessories, home-decor, beauty/bath-body, beauty/wash-bags) and returned None for every one. So no Bathroom leaf here collides with a previously validated workbook.
